new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Management - Platform
new_jobs.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue or San Francisco office location 4 days per week; Lambda's designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

About The Role

Every product Lambda ships depends on horizontal capabilities: the security and identity surfaces that let enterprise customers trust us, the telemetry and observability that tells us and our customers what the fleet is doing, and the metering and billing that turns per-minute GPU usage and committed cluster contracts into accurate invoices. When the platform layer is coherent, every Lambda product gets stronger at once. That is the leverage of this role.

You'll lead Lambda's Platform product group as a player-coach. You'll hire and manage three product managers, one each for Security, Observability, and Billing, all opening now. While you build that team, you'll personally own platform product strategy: the roadmap, the priorities, and the tradeoffs. You'll partner directly with platform engineering leadership. This is a first-line product management manager role, and you'll set the bar your team is measured against.

Great product managers at Lambda are defined by three things: insight, influence, and execution. Insight means you look at the data, determine what it means for customers and business, and then figure out what to do about it. But, a great idea doesn’t mean anything in a vacuum. That is where influence comes in. Influence means you take that idea and get others to want to buy into it; you win over engineers, designers, executives, and partners without relying on authority. But a great idea that everyone is excited about doesn’t matter unless it is delivered to customers. Execution means you work with the right people to get the idea launched, then measure and iterate. We hire product managers who learn new domains fast and reason rigorously from evidence. Deep domain depth in cloud platforms makes you stronger, but insight, influence, and execution are the bar.

Success in this role looks like two things: a platform layer that enterprise customers can trust, and a hired, high-performing product management team that clears the bar you set. If you love building the connective tissue of a cloud, and you want to grow product managers while still doing the work yourself, we'd love to hear from you.

We value diverse backgrounds, experiences, and skills, and we are excited to hear from candidates who can bring unique perspectives to our team. If you do not exactly meet this description but believe you may be a good fit, please still apply and help us understand your readiness for this role.

What You'll Do

Build the Team: Hire, manage, and develop the Security, Observability, and Billing product managers, and set the standard for insight, influence, and execution across the Platform product group.
Own the Roadmap: Define and own the platform roadmap end to end across security, observability, and billing, and hold it accountable to customer and business outcomes.
Carry the Strategy Yourself: Personally own platform product strategy while the team is being hired, so the roadmap never waits on headcount.
Strengthen Every Product: Deliver horizontal capabilities that On-Demand GPU Instances, 1-Click Clusters, and the Lambda Cloud API all depend on, rather than one-off features for a single product line.
Get Metering and Billing Right: Own the product surface for usage-based GPU compute billing, from per-minute on-demand billing to committed multi-node cluster contracts, so every invoice is accurate and explainable.
Earn Enterprise Trust: Shape the identity and security surfaces that let enterprise ML (machine learning) teams adopt Lambda with confidence.
Partner with Platform Engineering: Work side by side with platform engineering leadership on sequencing, tradeoffs, and delivery, so strategy and architecture move together.
Decide with Data: Turn fleet telemetry, usage patterns, and customer signal into clear build decisions, and communicate the what, the so what, and the now what to executives and customers.

You

Have 10+ years of product management experience, including experience shipping platform or infrastructure products that other teams build on
Have 3+ years hiring and managing product managers, or have formally led product managers as a first-line manager
Turn ambiguous data and customer signal into a clear decision about what to build next, and can show where you've done it
Win engineers, designers, executives, and customers over to your ideas without relying on organizational authority
Work with the right people to get products launched, then measure and iterate rather than moving on
Are comfortable operating as a player-coach, owning strategy directly while building the team that will own it after you
Can go deep with engineering leadership on technical tradeoffs and hold your own in architecture discussions
Communicate in writing clearly enough that an executive can act on your document without a follow-up meeting
Able to define iterative plans that move an organization from the current state towards the desired outcome

Nice to Have

Have shipped metering, billing, or monetization systems for usage-based products
Have built identity, security, or compliance product surfaces for enterprise customers
Have built telemetry or observability products, or worked deeply with tools like Prometheus and Grafana
Have a background in GPU compute, high performance computing, or AI infrastructure
Have built a product team from zero, including writing the job descriptions and running the hiring loops

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

About Lambda

Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast
Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove
We have research papers accepted at top machine learning and graphics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, and TOG
Our values are publicly available: https://lambda.ai/careers
We offer generous cash & equity compensation
Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents
Wellness and commuter stipends for select roles
401k Plan with 2% company match (USA employees)
Flexible paid time off plan that we all actually use

Equal Opportunity Employer

Lambda is an Equal Opportunity employer. Applicants are considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, gender, marital status, sexual orientation and identity, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other factors prohibited by local, state, or federal law.

Compensation Range: $365K - $540K

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, eDiscovery Technology
new_jobs.description:
About the role

KLDiscovery brings clarity, trust, and meaning to data for clients navigating legal matters worldwide. The eDiscovery Technology practice is where those clients meet advanced analytics and AI: technology-assisted review, generative AI classification for relevance and privilege, search and analytics strategy, and the non-standard workflows that turn a hard matter into a defensible, efficient one. Clients across the US, UK, Europe, and Asia Pacific are asking how to use AI in discovery and how to defend it, each under their own rules. This practice answers them everywhere KLD operates.
The Senior Director, eDiscovery Technology leads that practice globally. You will lead a team of technologists and consultants across time zones, own the methodology and defensibility of every AI-assisted workflow we deliver, partner with Advisory to package and price the consulting offerings they sell, and sit at the table with Product and Engineering as we build AI review into our own platform. This is applied legal technology leadership rather than a software engineering role, and a legal background is preferred.

What you will do

Lead the eDiscovery Technology practice

Lead a team of eDiscovery technologists and consultants who design and run advanced analytics and AI-assisted workflows on client matters, including technology-assisted review and continuous active learning, generative AI review for relevance and privilege, search and analytics strategy, and custom workflow design for non-standard tools and data.
Run the practice on a billable model: request intake, scoping, staffing, utilization, quality, and turnaround, against a demand curve that is growing fast.
Run it as one global practice, with one intake, one standard, and one set of playbooks across the US, EMEA, and APAC. Build follow-the-sun handoffs so a matter started in London or Hong Kong is picked up cleanly in the US, and partner with regional Operations leaders on staffing, skills, and coverage.
Grow the practice. Hire, onboard, and develop a manager, consultants, and technologists as demand expands, and build a career path from technologist to consultant to lead.
Build the operating rhythm: intake standards, capacity forecasting, coverage for second-shift, weekend, and deadline-driven work, quality standards, and playbooks so every matter gets the same standard regardless of who staffs it.

Own the methodology and its defensibility

Own how KLD applies analytics and AI to review: TAR 1.0 and 2.0, continuous active learning, generative AI classifiers for relevance and privilege, prompt design and iteration, validation statistics (recall, precision, elusion), and the documentation that makes the result defensible.
Serve as the senior subject matter expert for clients and counsel on AI-assisted review: scoping, protocol support, validation design, and explaining results in plain language to lawyers who have to sign their name to them.
Build reusable playbooks, prompt libraries, validation templates, and reporting so quality lives in the practice rather than in any one person.
Own AI governance for client matters with Legal and InfoSec: client data boundaries, client-specific AI restrictions, privilege protections, and audit trail, applied consistently across every tool the practice uses.
Adapt the methodology to the jurisdiction without lowering the standard: US TAR and GenAI case law and protocols, UK disclosure practice, GDPR and UK data protection, cross-border transfer and data residency limits, and APAC requirements, so the same playbook is defensible in every region where we run it.

Co-own the consulting offerings with Advisory

Partner with Advisory and Sales to define, package, and price the AI and analytics consulting offerings they sell: what we offer, how it is scoped, what it costs to deliver, and what margin it carries.
Supply the technical authority in pursuits Advisory leads across regions: pre-sales calls, RFP responses, pilots, and client education sessions for US, UK, European, and APAC clients and law firms.
Move the practice from reactive technical support toward productized consulting with clear deliverables, pricing, and outcomes.
Track offering revenue, attach rate, billable utilization, revenue per consultant per week, and margin, and report them into the weekly and monthly business reviews.

Partner with Product and Engineering

Serve as the practice’s voice into KLD’s own AI review capabilities: requirements, pilot design, operational readiness, adoption, and the feedback loop from client matters back to the roadmap.
Evaluate and adopt third-party analytics and AI tools, run structured comparisons, and own the practice’s vendor relationships and licensing.
Work with Process Engineering to encode repeatable workflows into automation and AI skills so the team’s time goes to judgment rather than mechanics.

Lead clients and cross-functional partners

Act as the senior technical voice for Client Success, Sales, and clients in every region on complex matters, escalations, and methodology questions, including cross-border matters that span more than one jurisdiction.
Represent the practice externally with a clear point of view on AI in discovery, thought leadership, and industry presence.
Lead with KLD’s values: Client is Always in the Room, Better Every Day, Own the Outcome, and Deliver Results Together.

What you will Bring

Required

10+ years in eDiscovery or litigation technology, including 5+ years applying advanced analytics and AI-assisted review on client matters and 3+ years leading a team.
Deep hands-on expertise in TAR 1.0 and 2.0, continuous active learning, and generative AI review (Relativity aiR, eDiscovery AI, or equivalent), including prompt design, validation statistics, and defensibility documentation. Working command of Relativity and RelativityOne.
A client-facing record: you have scoped, defended, and explained AI-assisted review to counsel and clients, supported protocol negotiations, and handled the hard questions.
Multi-jurisdiction experience: you have delivered analytics or AI-assisted review on matters outside the US or for non-US clients, and you understand GDPR, cross-border data transfer constraints, and how disclosure practice in the UK, EU, or APAC differs from US discovery.
Commercial fluency: you have packaged or priced consulting work, partnered with sales on pursuits, and can explain utilization and margin to a CFO.
Product partnership experience as the operational or practitioner voice on AI feature design, pilots, or adoption.
A record of building and developing a technical consulting team, including growing leads into managers and leading people across time zones.
A direct, clear communication style. You can explain recall and elusion to a general counsel and to a first-year technologist in the same afternoon.
Experience in PE-backed or high-growth environments where pace and accountability are the norm.

Preferred

Legal degree (JD or equivalent); bar admission a plus.
Structured analytics experience (Brainspace, Reveal, or similar).
Declaration or testimony experience on review methodology.
Relativity certifications, CEDS, or equivalent.

Our mission and core values:
We bring clarity, trust, and meaning to data for clients navigating legal matters worldwide.

Client is Always in the Room.
We operate and make decisions as if the client is in the room. We anticipate their needs, consider their perspective, and prioritize their best interests.

Better Every Day.
We improve our tomorrow by always striving to be better than today. We embrace curiosity, question assumptions, and raise the bar constantly.

Own the Outcome.
We bring an unwavering bias for action, act with urgency, and hold ourselves accountable to our clients and each other.

Deliver Results Together.
We collaborate obsessively to achieve shared success. We assume good intentions, debate ideas thoughtfully, treat each other with respect, and fully commit once decisions are made.

Our culture shapes our actions, our products, and the relationships we forge with our customers.

new_jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
new_jobs.description:
Overview

The IT Director provides enterprise-level leadership for BerryDunn’s technology strategy, operations, and modernization efforts in support of a geographically distributed workforce, multiple office locations, and the firm’s continued growth. This role shapes the vision and direction for IT infrastructure, enterprise systems, business applications, architecture, data platforms, and digital transformation, ensuring technology capabilities enable strategic priorities, operational effectiveness, service reliability, and future growth. Leading the IT Leadership Team, the IT Director serves as a strategic business leader, leveraging technology, data, automation, and artificial intelligence to strengthen client service, improve operational scalability and employee experience, and support the firm’s long-term growth.

Travel Expectations:
This role requires minimal travel, less than 10% per year.

You Will

Lead the development and execution of a multi-year IT strategic and operational plan that positions IT as a proactive partner in firm growth, transformation, service excellence, and operational effectiveness.
Establish IT goals, governance practices, service expectations, and performance measures that strengthen accountability, reliability, and operational excellence.
Develop and manage annual operating and capital budgets, technology forecasts, business cases, sourcing strategies, vendor investments, and multi-year investment roadmaps that optimize firm value, cost effectiveness, resource capacity, and service quality.
Establish enterprise architecture practices, including technology standards, solution design governance, integration patterns, platform roadmaps, and technical debt management.
Oversee internal systems, enterprise applications, data platforms, integrations, and databases to ensure solutions are secure, scalable, reliable, maintainable, and aligned with firm architecture standards.
Lead evaluation, governance, and adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, automation, and productivity platforms, to improve business outcomes while aligning with risk, cybersecurity, data protection, and compliance requirements.
Advance observability and performance insight across IT systems, including service health, application performance, incident trends, availability, reliability, and KPI reporting.
Partner with firm leaders and transformation stakeholders to prioritize and deliver technology initiatives that improve client service, operational efficiency, automation, digital enablement, and business outcomes.
Collaborate with cybersecurity, risk, compliance, and business continuity stakeholders to align technology decisions with security requirements, data protection expectations, and firm risk priorities.
Partner with business leaders to govern technology demand, prioritize the IT portfolio, and balance resource capacity, business value, risk, and strategic objectives.
Lead technology-enabled change by building stakeholder alignment and readiness and coordinating communication, training, adoption, and sustained use of new systems and tools.
Promote continuous learning and innovation across IT through knowledge sharing, technical development, communities of practice, and ongoing capability building.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Lead and develop the IT Leadership Team, fostering a culture of empowerment, collaboration, innovation, and accountability.
Oversee recruitment, development, retention, and succession planning for IT staff.
Define, communicate, and engage others in strategic plans, policies, and technology standards across all levels of the firm.
Build and maintain strategic relationships with external partners, vendors, and industry associations to enhance IT strategy and capabilities.

You Have

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
10-15 years of progressive IT leadership experience in a professional services or complex office environment, including experience leading managers, technical teams, vendors, contractors, and/or managed service providers.
Proven experience developing IT strategy, governance practices, technology roadmaps, and operational plans that align with business objectives.
Experience managing IT budgets, sourcing strategies, vendor relationships, contracts, statements of work, and service delivery expectations.
Experience leading enterprise applications, internal systems development, architecture, integration, database, data platform, or cloud-based technology teams.
Working knowledge of modern IT practices, including SDLC, project management, service management, data governance, cybersecurity, cloud platforms, and secure configuration practices.
Experience with observability, monitoring, IT service analytics, operational dashboards, and KPI-based performance management.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional transformation initiatives with measurable business outcomes.
Relevant technical, ITIL, project management, cloud, or security-related certifications valued.

Compensation Details

The base salary range targeted for this role is $185,000 - $210,000. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based on factors such as company and personal performance. This salary range represents BerryDunn’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. If an applicant possesses experience, education, or other qualifications more than the minimum requirements for this posting, that applicant is encouraged to apply, and a final salary range may then be based on those additional qualifications; compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to years of experience, depth of experience, seniority, merit, education, training, amount of travel, and other relevant business considerations.

BerryDunn Benefits & Culture

Our people are what make BerryDunn special, and in return we strive to support our employees and help them thrive. Eligible employees have access to benefits that go beyond what’s expected to support their physical, mental, career, social, and financial well-being. Visit our website for a complete list of benefits and a look into our culture: Experience BerryDunn .

We will ensure that individuals are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process or perform essential job functions. Please contact careers@berrydunn.com to request an accommodation.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

About BerryDunn

BerryDunn is the brand name under which Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC and BDMP Assurance, LLP, independently owned entities, provide services. Since 1974, BerryDunn has helped businesses, nonprofits, and government agencies throughout the US and its territories solve their greatest challenges. The firm’s tax, advisory, and consulting services are provided by Berry, Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC, and its attest services are provided by BDMP Assurance, LLP, a licensed CPA firm.

BerryDunn is a client-centered, people-first professional services firm with a mission to empower the meaningful growth of our people, clients, and communities. The firm has been recognized for its efforts in creating a diverse and inclusive workplace culture, and for its focus on learning, development, and well-being. Learn more at berrydunn.com .

new_jobs.title: Vice President of Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Paperless Parts is the SaaS-based intelligence layer for modern manufacturing, enabling our customers to innovate faster in the physical world. From rockets to medical devices, we power the parts that move the world forward.

Location:
Boston, MA (Hybrid) Reports To:
Chief Technology Officer Employment Type:
Full-Time Travel:
5–10%

This position requires activities that are subject to US Export Control Laws and require US Citizenship or Green Card Holder.

The Opportunity

Four years ago Paperless Parts was a startup. Today it's a scale-up with an engineering team that ships reliably, a platform that's changing how manufacturers quote and run their business, and a customer base that keeps growing. The next chapter is new product lines and faster growth, and we need a VP of Engineering to lead that shift. You'll report to the CTO and run a 25+ person organization through two Directors of Engineering, working as a peer to the VP of Product and Chief Scientist. The job is two jobs at once: keep the core platform stable and improving for customers who depend on it daily, while standing up new products in a market where AI is changing what's possible to build and how fast you can build it. Whoever takes this on has to be good at both, and has to make the team better at both.

What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months)

The next product line is in market, with real customers live on it and generating revenue, on a platform built to scale; proof Paperless Parts can build a second product the market wants, not just defend the first one.
The team has moved from using AI inside the SDLC to running an AI-native SDLC, one built on a first-class engineering culture, with people still at the center of how software gets made.
Successful delivery means customer value landed, not tickets closed; Engineering and Product move as one team toward customer-facing measure of success.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Operations:
Own engineering delivery, quality, and predictability, establishing an operational rhythm the broader company depends on.
Technical Direction:
Own the architecture and platform decisions that set our foundation for the next stage. New products mean new architecture, and the choices made now set the tone for how we build for years to come.
Product Partnership:
Partner with the VP of Product on a roadmap that delivers real value to customers, sharing ownership of sequencing, trade-offs, and the commitments we make. Engineering brings feasibility, cost, and options to the table early, not after the plan is set.
Manufacturing Intelligence:
Partner with the Chief Scientist on the development and execution of our manufacturing intelligence strategy, bringing new AI-driven capability to market.
AI Leverage:
We have adopted AI across the engineering organization. Lead the next step: maximize its leverage to shape how we work for the future, while holding the line on quality.
Platform Efficiency:
Keep the core platform cheaper to run, faster to change, and more reliable as customer volume grows.
Leadership and Team Growth:
Coach Directors and Engineering Managers, establish clear career paths that develop and retain strong engineers, and direct the hiring plan and selection standard so the team grows without compromising technical or cultural quality.
Executive Leadership:
Represent engineering status, capacity, risks, and strategic tradeoffs clearly to the executive leadership team.

Qualifications & Experience

Core Requirements

Scale Experience:
Demonstrated track record of leading multi-team B2B SaaS engineering organizations through growth phases while continuously improving delivery quality and predictability.
Management Depth:
Proven success managing through Directors and Engineering Managers, with evidence of developing frontline leaders.
Modern SaaS Architecture:
Deep technical background in cloud-native platforms, with a track record of architectural decisions that scale under increasing customer load.
AI in Practice:
Experience raising an engineering team's effectiveness with AI tooling and AI-enabled product capability, with a clear point of view on where it works and where it does not.
Product Alignment:
Strong experience partnering with Product leadership to align technical roadmap priorities with commercial objectives.
Location:
US-based (Boston, MA hybrid).

Preferred Qualifications

New Product Execution:
Hands-on experience taking new product lines from early customer traction to scaled commercial production within an established organization.
Domain & Compliance Awareness:
Experience operating within security-conscious software environments (FedRAMP, etc.) or industrial/manufacturing SaaS sectors.

Salary range:

$215,000 - $310,000 base salary. This role is also eligible for a competitive variable bonus and equity opportunity

The job posting range is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, sales or revenue-based metrics, and business or organizational needs.

Paperless Parts Life

Culture:
At Paperless Parts, we value intentionality, persistence and relationships. We live and breathe these values every day. As a fast-growing company, we're continually improving what we've built while still building from the ground up.

Boston Office:
Our office is full of energy; people regularly collaborate to solve complex problems. We recognize that people work well in different environments and have intentionally designed our office to provide collaborative spaces and quiet focus areas. Our height-adjustable desks are set up with additional monitors, and employees are provided with the latest Apple technology to support productivity.

Our headquarters is located in downtown Boston, MA and easily accessible to most transit routes (Red/Blue/Orange/Green Line/South Station/North Station).

Encinitas Office:
Our California office is our newest office which seats our West Coast sales team. The office has an open floor plan with several conference rooms to encourage collaboration with your colleagues in California and TV's to connect with those sitting in Boston or remotely. new_jobs.description:
Paperless Parts is the SaaS-based intelligence layer for modern manufacturing, enabling our customers to innovate faster in the physical world. From rockets to medical devices, we power the parts that move the world forward.

Location:

5–10%

This position requires activities that are subject to US Export Control Laws and require US Citizenship or Green Card Holder.

The Opportunity

Four years ago Paperless Parts was a startup. Today it's a scale-up with an engineering team that ships reliably, a platform that's changing how manufacturers quote and run their business, and a customer base that keeps growing. The next chapter is new product lines and faster growth, and we need a VP of Engineering to lead that shift. You'll report to the CTO and run a 25+ person organization through two Directors of Engineering, working as a peer to the VP of Product and Chief Scientist. The job is two jobs at once: keep the core platform stable and improving for customers who depend on it daily, while standing up new products in a market where AI is changing what's possible to build and how fast you can build it. Whoever takes this on has to be good at both, and has to make the team better at both.

What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months)

The next product line is in market, with real customers live on it and generating revenue, on a platform built to scale; proof Paperless Parts can build a second product the market wants, not just defend the first one.
The team has moved from using AI inside the SDLC to running an AI-native SDLC, one built on a first-class engineering culture, with people still at the center of how software gets made.
Successful delivery means customer value landed, not tickets closed; Engineering and Product move as one team toward customer-facing measure of success.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Operations: Own engineering delivery, quality, and predictability, establishing an operational rhythm the broader company depends on.
Technical Direction: Own the architecture and platform decisions that set our foundation for the next stage. New products mean new architecture, and the choices made now set the tone for how we build for years to come.
Product Partnership: Partner with the VP of Product on a roadmap that delivers real value to customers, sharing ownership of sequencing, trade-offs, and the commitments we make. Engineering brings feasibility, cost, and options to the table early, not after the plan is set.
Manufacturing Intelligence: Partner with the Chief Scientist on the development and execution of our manufacturing intelligence strategy, bringing new AI-driven capability to market.
AI Leverage: We have adopted AI across the engineering organization. Lead the next step: maximize its leverage to shape how we work for the future, while holding the line on quality.
Platform Efficiency: Keep the core platform cheaper to run, faster to change, and more reliable as customer volume grows.
Leadership and Team Growth: Coach Directors and Engineering Managers, establish clear career paths that develop and retain strong engineers, and direct the hiring plan and selection standard so the team grows without compromising technical or cultural quality.
Executive Leadership: Represent engineering status, capacity, risks, and strategic tradeoffs clearly to the executive leadership team.

Qualifications & Experience

Core Requirements

Scale Experience: Demonstrated track record of leading multi-team B2B SaaS engineering organizations through growth phases while continuously improving delivery quality and predictability.
Management Depth: Proven success managing through Directors and Engineering Managers, with evidence of developing frontline leaders.
Modern SaaS Architecture: Deep technical background in cloud-native platforms, with a track record of architectural decisions that scale under increasing customer load.
AI in Practice: Experience raising an engineering team's effectiveness with AI tooling and AI-enabled product capability, with a clear point of view on where it works and where it does not.
Product Alignment: Strong experience partnering with Product leadership to align technical roadmap priorities with commercial objectives.
Location: US-based (Boston, MA hybrid).

Preferred Qualifications

New Product Execution: Hands-on experience taking new product lines from early customer traction to scaled commercial production within an established organization.
Domain & Compliance Awareness: Experience operating within security-conscious software environments (FedRAMP, etc.) or industrial/manufacturing SaaS sectors.

Salary range:

$215,000 - $310,000 base salary. This role is also eligible for a competitive variable bonus and equity opportunity

At Paperless Parts, we value intentionality, persistence and relationships. We live and breathe these values every day. As a fast-growing company, we’re continually improving what we’ve built while still building from the ground up.
